10045879:
Derek Grivois Gateway Snowmobile Club - Van Buren LD 1547
April 23, 2025
Greetings,
As President of the Gateway Snowmobile Club in Van Buren Maine. I am writing on behalf of our club in full support of bill LD 1547 "An Act to Use a Portion of the Sales Tax on Snowmobiles to Fund Maine's Snowmobile Trail Programs". This act would benefit all clubs throughout the state and especially our clubs in Aroostook County. Maine Snowmobile clubs throughout the state which are volunteer, rely on various income sources for basic operations. Currently, the state grant is set to return 70% of our total operating costs for a season which helps us cover basic expenses but, does not leave much room for any equipment purchases/upgrades or trails in need of maintenance and or repairs. Every year we struggle to even groom our 80 miles in trails as our budgets are under constant strain from unexpected costs. Ask yourself this, if you run a business and only received 70% of your operating costs in return with no other help how long would it survive? It is especially difficult in NORTHERN Maine as our season is always longer than the rest of the State.
Currently, our club is in the process of soliciting funds to construct a garage/maintenance building for 2 groomers. The current shed which was constructed in the early 1900's has deteriorated to the point of no return. This is a $300,000 project and as of this date and the gracious donations of various sources and fund raisers, we have secured about $100,000 which will at least give us a start. Another issue for us is an aging groomer which is in desperate need of 2 tracks which has a price tag of $38,000. We have not been able to purchase the tracks due to insufficient funds. We were lucky to use that machine this past year without a catastrophic failure but, will have to either find the funding to repair it or sideline it for the next season. Trails are another issue; they constantly need attention to provide a SAFE RIDING EXPERIENCE for riders which costs clubs more in funds sometimes unexpectedly.
In conclusion, the State of Maine needs to do a better job in helping snowmobile clubs provide safe riding trails for all snowmobilers. We have some of the most pristine trails in the country which draws in tourists from all over! At the current rate, we are finding it more difficult to keep up financially and need help! Please help us help the State in working together in making the snowmobiling experience a safe a rememberable one! This proposed bill is a step in the RIGHT direction, please PASS it! As a side note, why doesn't the State REQUIRE all registered snowmobiles to join a club to ride the maintained trail system?....food for thought.
Sincerely,
Derek Grivois, President GSC

o 2023-24 season was $582 million dollars (in 2024 dollars)

This economic impact provided by volunteers and funded by State trail grant programs only receive funds from snowmobile registrations in the amount of $3,045,743 (2023-2024) and 0.87% or $1,530,072 (2023-2024) from gas tax.
2019-2023 Municipal & Club In-Aid grants only funded 59% of reported expenses, this still
left a $2.66 million short fall of the club's reported cost.

2019-2023 Capitol Equipment In~Aid grants funded 24% of the equipment c0st,$13.4
million shortfall of the total equipment cost. This funding formula is no longer working for our clubs. They need more funding.

10045999:
TESTIMONY OF MICHAEL J. ALLEN, ASSOCIATE COMMISSIONER FOR TAX POLICY
DEPARTMENT OF ADMINISTRATIVE AND FINANCIAL SERVICES
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Taxation Hearing Date: April 23, 2025, Wednesday at 1:00 P.M.
LD 1547 - "An Act to Use a Portion of the Sales Tax on Snowmobiles to Fund Maine's Snowmobile Trail Programs"
Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and members of the Taxation Committee - good afternoon, my name is Michael Allen, Associate Commissioner for Tax Policy in the Department of Administrative and Financial Services. I am testifying at the request of the Administration Against LD 1547, "An Act to Use a Portion of the Sales Tax on Snowmobiles to Fund Maine's Snowmobile Trail Programs."
This bill requires 40% of sales and use tax revenue collected with respect to snowmobiles to be credited to the Snowmobile Trail Fund of the Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry, Bureau of Parks and Lands.
Currently, the Department of Inland Fisheries and Wildlife (IFW) is responsible for collecting the use tax due with respect to watercraft, snowmobiles, and all-terrain vehicles (ATVs) for which an original registration is required. IFW provides a monthly report to MRS to identify the amount of use tax it collected on watercraft, snowmobiles and ATVs, which MRS staff then credits to the General Fund.
To facilitate the transfer proposed in this bill, MRS would need to add a line to both the use tax return and the sales tax return, specific to reporting the tax on
1

sales of snowmobiles; 40% of the total amount reported on those lines would be transferred to the Snowmobile Trail Fund.
The casual sale of a snowmobile to a nonresident individual, however, is exempt from use tax, meaning IFW would not collect use tax on the registration of a snowmobile, purchased at casual sale, by a nonresident pursuant to 36 M.R.S. � 1760(25-C). These sales would generate no revenue for the fund.
Turning to technical concerns, the bill should be amended to include an effective date. The committee should also note that the same sales tax receipts are included in the 5% transfer to the Local Government Fund (without any reduction) pursuant to 30-A M.R.S. � 5681(5). As such, the bill should state whether the Snowmobile Trail Fund transfer amount equals 40% of those sales tax receipts before or after they are reduced by the Local Government Fund transfer amount. Further, the bill should specify the timing and frequency of required transfers, and that the amount transferred must be certified by the State Tax Assessor. For model language, see 36 M.R.S. � 1821 (requiring that certain automobile-related sales and use tax revenue be transferred to the Local Government Fund prior to the Highway Fund).
This bill appears to be patterned on the current transfer of 40% of the 5.5% sales tax remitted by new and used automobile dealers licensed by the Bureau of Motor Vehicles and use tax collected by municipalities from casual sales to the Highway Fund. Adding a line to the sales tax return to breakout sales of snowmobiles will complicate what has historically been a relatively easy tax return for retailers to complete.
2

If the Committee seeks to allocate additional funds to the Snowmobile Trail Fund, it should do so as a direct appropriation rather than dedicating 40% of sales tax revenue from snowmobile sales.
The fiscal impact estimate is not available at this time. The administrative cost estimate is not available at this time. The Administration looks forward to working with the Committee on the bill; representatives from MRS will be here for the Work Session to provide additional information and respond in detail to the Committee's questions.

Senator Grohoski, Representative Cloutier, and members of the Taxation Committee:
I am Russell Black and I have the pleasure of representing Senate District 5. I am here
today to introduce LD 1547, "An Act to Use a Portion of the Sales Tax on Snowmobiles to
Fund Maine's Snowmobile Trail Programs."
In recent years I have spoken to many snowmobile club volunteers about the need to increase funding for local clubs to be able to maintain Maine's vast network of snowmobile trails. This need was never more apparent than after the experience
snowmobile clubs had following the historic winter storms of 2023/2024.
I am pleased to have been able to work with the Maine Snowmobile Association on
this legislation and propose a funding model that is similar to that of motor vehicles
and public roads. In this case, we propose to dedicate 40% of the sales tax on
snowmobiles to the State's Snowmobile Trail Fund.
As you know, snowmobiling in Maine is a longstanding family tradition, and helps to attract hundreds of millions of dollars to our local economies. The dwindling active
volunteers at local snowmobile clubs shoulder the burden of keeping these trails in extraordinary condition, both for resident riders and visitors alike. Counting on volunteers to do these jobs is one thing, but counting on them to do this job without
adequate resources is something we have the ability to avoid.
Now, I recognize that Maine's fiscal condition is lean and we all have tough choices to make when it comes to how we will spend remaining state dollars; but I ask you to
consider this model and see if there might be ways to begin moving the needle in a way that helps provide more adequate funding for these local clubs in a manner that is
reflective of how much value they create for Maine's winter economy.

Thank you for your consideration.
